tasks.title: Auth persistence and settings foundations
tasks.objective: Add the durable auth data model, settings shape, repository primitives, and trusted identity attestation needed by every later browser-auth path.
acceptance_criteria: Postgres migrations and repositories cover local authorization codes, OIDC transactions, browser sessions, console access grants, and invitations.
All reusable tokens and references are stored as hashes only, one-use records are consumed atomically, and the final active Administrator invariant is transactionally enforced.
Authentication settings add local or hosted mode, canonical origin, generic OIDC candidate and active configuration, and client-secret references without changing runtime.deployment_mode.
OIDC issuer plus subject aliases and verified email aliases reuse the existing Person and user_aliases model; email never selects or silently links a Person.

tasks.title: Browser server trust boundary and local authorization
tasks.objective: Add the reusable browser trust-boundary policy for local authorization: cookie semantics, CSRF and canonical-origin checks, loopback recognition, and an exhaustive browser-role scope map.
acceptance_criteria: Browser and Bearer credentials are mutually exclusive; browser session and CSRF cookies use the required local and hosted attributes, and authentication responses are no-store capable.
Browser mutations can require exact canonical Origin plus a synchronizer CSRF token, while local browser authorization recognizes only loopback hosts.
Every Control scope is classified as Administrator, Viewer-safe read, or browser-ineligible, with Viewer access read-only by policy.

browser scope policy > classifies every Control scope and keeps Viewer read-only

review_budget.reason: Pure shared policy boundary with direct unit proof.

tasks.title: Hosted OIDC, grants, invitations, and reauthentication
tasks.objective: Implement hosted sign-in, provider-neutral OIDC validation, invitation binding, access-state handling, reauthentication, and session rotation.
acceptance_criteria: OIDC start/callback/reauth validates discovery issuer, allowlist, state, nonce, PKCE, signature, audience, expiry, and callback replay using DNS-pinned transport and jose.
Google company-domain identities get Viewer access, other identities require invitation or explicit approval, and disabled or unapproved users receive the exact approved safe copy.
Invitations are fragment-token, one-use, hash-only, expire after seven days, match only the verified normalized invited email, and bind durable identity by issuer plus subject.
Hosted sessions use the approved __Host cookie, two-hour idle and 12-hour absolute lifetimes, warn five minutes before absolute expiry, and rotate after login, reauth, and role elevation.
Reauthentication uses a 10-minute recent-authentication window, returns the exact approved success copy, and never replays the pending mutation automatically.

tasks.title: Auth operations, audit events, and documentation
tasks.objective: Add the required CLI operations, safe audit events, candidate OIDC test and activation behavior, and operator documentation.
acceptance_criteria: gantry ui and gantry ui authorize create local authorization links, and gantry auth access approve <reference> --role administrator|viewer writes the grant and audit event transactionally after confirmation.
First-admin and lost-admin access references expire after 15 minutes and are stored as hashes on awaiting grants.
OIDC candidate testing never changes active runtime behavior, failed tests preserve active configuration, and activation promotes the candidate through settings revisions.

Audit events cover login classification, logout, revocation, invitations, access and role changes, reauthentication, configuration activation, and CLI recovery without tokens, raw claims, secrets, PKCE verifiers, or upstream errors.
Docs cover local startup, hosted proxy and cache requirements, setup, first-admin approval, lost-admin recovery, and broken-OIDC recovery.

tasks.title: Authentication and Access web UI
tasks.objective: Add public auth pages, protected session-aware shell loading, and the approved Settings to Authentication and Access experience using existing React primitives.
acceptance_criteria: Public local authorization, hosted sign-in, invitation, callback failure, no-access, disabled-access, retry, setup, and reauthentication screens use the exact approved copy.
The AppShell is protected by session-aware route loading, while public auth routes live outside the shell.

Settings to Authentication and Access shows the approved adaptive local and hosted tabs, Administrator and Viewer roles only, invitations, access administration, session management, OIDC setup, receipts, and final-admin error behavior.
The UI preserves existing dialogs, tables, fields, stale-data behavior, focus restoration, keyboard navigation, theme tokens, responsive behavior, and reduced-motion support.
Viewer restrictions are server-enforced and reflected in the UI without converting unrelated fixture-backed console features to live APIs.

tasks.title: Integrated auth verification and cleanup proof
tasks.objective: Prove the full browser-auth boundary with focused and full verification, security cleanup searches, autoreview, and the required functional check.
acceptance_criteria: Unit, OIDC contract, disposable-Postgres integration, HTTP boundary, CLI, and web tests cover the approved lifetimes, copy, role behavior, replay rejection, cookie flags, CSRF/origin checks, final-admin invariant, safe errors, and Viewer restrictions.
Cleanup searches prove there is no email-keyed identity, first-user-wins branch, browser Bearer credential, /auth/recover, recovery cookie/session, raw token logging, or mock-only Operator role.

Core and web format, lint, typecheck, build, architecture checks, migration checks, disposable-Postgres suites, and python3 factory/scripts/verify.py complete or report explicit environment-limited gaps.
One autoreview pass covers quality, performance, and security, and the required functional-checker flow is completed because the feature is user-facing.
